advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm skipping confirmed bindings with missing/blank jira_key is intended, or route them to a store-integrity/drift bucket instead of silently continuing.
evidence: bridge_fsck_drift.py: `jira_key = entry.get("jira_key")` then `if not isinstance(jira_key, str) or not jira_key: continue`

Old code (removed in diff) had no such guard: `jira_key = entry.get("jira_key")` followed directly by classification, so a confirmed binding with jira_key=None/'' was still classified (would_terminal/local_gone).
advisory.finding: Behavior change: audit_binding_drift now skips any confirmed binding whose jira_key is not a non-empty string ('if not isinstance(jira_key, str) or not jira_key: continue'), whereas the old code processed such entries (jira_key could be None/empty and still flow into local-decidable classification such as local_gone). A confirmed binding with a missing/blank jira_key is now silently dropped from all drift buckets.
scenarios: a confirmed binding whose jira_key was cleared or never set — previously flagged local_gone/would_terminal, now invisible

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `write_report_json` write `reconcile-check.json` atomically (temp file + `os.replace`) to match the sibling `_write_detail` store-write discipline and eliminate the torn-read window for the new cross-process `_read_reconcile_diagnostics` reader.
evidence: Shared resource: `.bridge_state/reconcile-check.json`

Writer executor (reconciler process): src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:272 `output_path = tracker_dir / ".bridge_state" / "reconcile-check.json"` then `rc_mod.write_report_json(report, output_path)`

Non-atomic WRITE: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile_check.py:422-423 `output_path.parent.mkdir(...)` / `output_path.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2, default=str) + "\n")` (in-place truncate+write, no temp+rename)
Reader executor (bridge_status process): src/rebar/_lib_ops.py:299 `result = last_pass.snapshot(...)` → src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/last_pass.py:328 `_read_reconcile_diagnostics(repo_root)`
READ: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/last_pass.py:210 `decoded = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))`

Sibling accessor + its guard (SAME module): `_write_detail` at src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/last_pass.py:338-343 writes via `tempfile.mkstemp(...)` then `os.replace(temporary, path)` — the atomic-rename discipline that makes its bare-read reader `_read_matching_detail` (last_pass.py:190) torn-read-safe; `write_report_json` omits this guard.

Harm disposition (for Pass-2 scoring): the torn read is caught by `except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError): return None` (last_pass.py:213-214), so the effect is fail-open — the optional `reconcile_diagnostics` field is transiently absent from one status snapshot and self-corrects next read; the parsed value is never partially corrupted and is not branched on or persisted. Benign-tolerant per the guard; the actionable defect is the missing atomic-write discipline vs the sibling writer.
advisory.finding: `reconcile-check.json` is written non-atomically by `write_report_json` (truncate-then-write `write_text`), but its new cross-process reader `_read_reconcile_diagnostics` in `bridge_status` reads it with a bare `read_text` — unlike the sibling store file in the same module, whose writer `_write_detail` uses the atomic `os.replace` discipline that makes its bare-read reader safe. A `bridge_status` call interleaving with a reconciler write can observe a partially written / truncated file.
scenarios: An MCP/CLI `bridge_status` call arrives while a reconciler pass is rewriting `reconcile-check.json`; the reader observes a truncated file and drops `reconcile_diagnostics` from that snapshot.
advisory.suggested_fix: In `reconcile_check.write_report_json`, write to a temp file in `output_path.parent` and `os.replace(tmp, output_path)` (mirroring `last_pass._write_detail`) instead of a bare `output_path.write_text(...)`.
